sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Clothra, or Clothru, was an Irish heroine or goddess. King Eochaid Fedlech had four famed daughters, Medb, Eithne, Mugain, plus Clothra, along with three sons who all bore the name Finn. Clothra gave her three brothers one son, Lugaidh Riab nDerg, whose body red stripes divided into three, each part mothered by a different brother in turn. Later she lay with that son and conceived Crimthann Nia Náir. Crimthann came into the world after his mother's death, for Medb, envious of her, killed her. The run of incest hints that Clothra began as an ancestral deity.

okr.objective: Clothra is a heroine whose children, born from her brothers, trace an ancestral goddess.
key_results: Clothra is a daughter of king Eochaid Fedlech.
Her son Lugaidh was sired by her three brothers.
